question: Who among the following is the first African woman to assume office as the Commonwealth Secretary General in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shirley Botchwey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey** is a Ghanaian politician and diplomat who has held significant positions in government, including serving as the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration in Ghana since 2017.
 
• She is the first African woman to assume the position of the Commonwealth Secretary General, starting her term in April 2025, making history in the organization's leadership.
 
• The Commonwealth Secretary General leads the Commonwealth Secretariat, which is responsible for implementing the decisions and policies of the Commonwealth Heads of Government.
 
• Shirley Botchwey has been recognized for her extensive experience in diplomacy, governance, and international relations, which contributed to her selection for this prestigious role.
 
• The Commonwealth is an intergovernmental organization of 56 member states, most of which are former territories of the British Empire, and its leadership represents a diverse and global community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tansu Çiller**:

 
 
• She is a Turkish economist and politician who served as the Prime Minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996, becoming the first and only woman to hold this position in Turkey.
 
• Çiller led Turkey during a period of significant economic reform and was involved in key diplomatic efforts regarding Turkey's relations with the European Union and NATO.
 
 
 
• **Hanna Suchocka**:
 
 
• She is a Polish politician and lawyer who served as the Prime Minister of Poland from 1992 to 1993, becoming the first woman to hold this office in Poland.
 
• Suchocka played a critical role in Poland's transition from communism to democracy and worked to implement economic reforms during her tenure.
 
 
 
• **Sylvie Kinigi**:
 
 
• She is a Burundian politician who served as the Prime Minister of Burundi from 1993 to 1994, becoming the first woman to hold this position in the country.
 
• Kinigi's tenure came during a turbulent time in Burundi's history, marked by political instability and ethnic conflict.
